**Question**

My youngest brother Joshua likes to play with bricks. One day he makes the following shape using four bricks:

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i00.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i00.png")

If you look at this three-dimensional object from the three different directions indicated above, the shape looks like:

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i01.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i01.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i01.png")
![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i02.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i02.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i02.png")

The next day Joshua makes a different shape using six bricks:

![papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i04.png](/assets/papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i04.png "papers/the-haberdashers-askes-boys-school/2009/sample-paper-1/s01-q25-i04.png")

not necessarily whole numbers.
